title: Optimizing SFQ Circuit Design: A Timing-Driven Framework for Performance-Constrained Area Minimization
problem: Single Flux Quantum (SFQ) circuits face area overhead from path balancing and pipelining, compromising scalability despite high performance potential.
motivation: Optimized SFQ designs enabling area reduction without sacrificing throughput unlock practical applications at scale.
method: This framework designs SFQ circuits—a type of extremely fast superconducting circuit technology—by simultaneously optimizing three interconnected design decisions: which clock phase controls each part of the circuit, how to partition computation into pipeline stages, and how the signal distribution network is structured. It works by explicitly modeling the timing of each gate operation (measuring how long signals take to travel), then using efficient algorithms to find area-efficient designs without compromising speed, even for large circuits.
key_novelty: The core idea is using explicit timing information to jointly optimize path balancing (ensuring signals arrive together), clock phase assignment (choosing which clock phase controls each part), and the circuit area-performance tradeoff.
contributions: Timing-aware optimization framework modeling gate delays in SFQ circuits
Joint optimization of phase assignment, pipelining, and splitter construction
30% area and 29% latency reduction vs. traditional full path balancing at 27ps clock
22% lower area and 23% lower latency vs. prior multi-phase methods at tighter targets

metrics.area: 30% reduction vs. FPB; 22% vs. prior multi-phase at 21ps
metrics.other: 29% latency reduction at 27ps; 23% at 21ps clock period

limitations: Focused on benchmark circuits; practical SFQ system integration and cryogenic testing not demonstrated.
